subject: Dedicated capacity: multipool prioritization, regional fallbacks, and burst policy decisions
messages:

Cc: James O'Neill <james.oneill@galaxycloud.com>

Subject: Re: Initial sizing and timeline for dedicated GPU pools

Thanks Evelyn — appreciated the call today. We chatted internally and sketched out a couple of scenarios for launch. High level asks: (1) single region US-West with cold standby in US-East, (2) multipool for inference + batch (separate SKUs), and (3) predictable burst capacity for end-of-quarter spikes.

Can you confirm what level of autoscale granularity Redwood supports (per-model vs per-pool), and whether burst capacity is billed differently? Also attaching the rough traffic pattern we recorded (small file).

Priyanka

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the note and the traffic sheet. Short answers up front:
- Autoscale scope: Redwood supports autoscale at the pool level and model-route level (you can attach different autoscale policies to routes within a pool).
- Burst: burst capacity is configured per-pool and billed as metered burst units; we can set hard caps per-account to control cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik and I will propose a multipool draft (inference vs batch) with suggested GPU types for us-west/us-east.
2) Marissa will take the SOW redline and prepare a version for legal review.
3) Schedule a 60-minute handoff with your infra and security teams; please confirm availability next week.

I'll loop Sean for region capacity constraints.

-Evelyn

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-04-13T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing and timeline for dedicated GPU pools

Priyanka — dug into the traffic patterns you sent and sketched two deployment drafts:

Option A — Single-region primary (US-W) + standby (US-E):
- Inference pool: 8 x A800 (low-latency SLOs)
- Batch pool: 12 x A10G (cost-effective throughput)
- Burst policy: allow additional 4 A800-equivalent burst units in US-W for short spikes; 12-hr cooldown
- Failover: automated DR to US-E with cold-warm replication of KV cache

Option B — Multipool active/active (preferred for <2s p99):
- Two inference pools (US-W, US-E) 6 x A800 each, active/active with smart routing (latency policy)
- Batch in US-E primarily, with job spillover to US-W when idle
- Burst: pool-level burst buckets with per-deal cap (we can enforce at billing layer)

Tradeoffs callout: Option A reduces steady-state cost but increases recovery time for region outage. Option B improves p99 latency and gives lower cross-region failover complexity but costs more steady-state.

I attached a short sizing rationale (inline in the Drive folder). If you want, I can convert the outline into a provisioning checklist for Ops.

-Karthik
From: Priyanka Rao <pri@galaxycloud.com>

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from infra/security before we lock an option: 
1) For KV cache replication — what's the expected RTO for pulling a warm cache into a cold standby?
2) For burst billing — can we put an alerting threshold at 50% of the burst bucket to trigger manual approval for further spend?

Also James here will coordinate our legal/procurement side on SOW timelines. Can we get a draft SOW that preserves a per-pool cap and a dedicated escalation path?

-Priyanka
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Priyanka Rao <pri@galaxycloud.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial sizing and timeline for dedicated GPU pools

Priyanka — answered inline on the operational specifics: 
1) KV cache replication and RTO: For our standard cold-standby workflow, we expect a warm-up RTO of ~20–40 minutes to reach steady-state for most workloads; worst-case depend on model context size and cold-cache hit rates. For faster failover we recommend Option B or a hybrid where we pre-warm a fraction of cache (we can schedule pre-warms during business hours).
2) Burst manual approval: yes — we support a billing guardrail that raises an alert at a configurable percentage (we typically put the first alert at 50%) and requires an explicit approval to increase burst consumption beyond that. We can wire approvals to your internal ticketing (Jira) or mobile approvals.

Operational ask: please confirm your preferred option (A or B) and desired steady-state GPU types. We'll create the provisioning checklist and propose target dates once we have that.

-Sean
